agents.editable_prompt: Analyze the target US audience; distinguish measured audience signals from assumptions. Propose multiple Japanese history/culture topics with citations, uncertainty, a clear opening hook, and a falsifiable retention hypothesis. Reject near-duplicate and low-evidence concepts.

Turn the selected topic into an American-English short with a compelling question in the first three seconds, accurate context, a clear reveal, and satisfying payoff. Annotate each narrative beat and predicted retention mechanism; avoid unverifiable drama.
Fact-check key claims against trustworthy historical sources. Provide evidence references and classify ambiguity honestly; report insufficient rather than inventing citations.
Review historical accuracy, hook clarity, narration, scene transitions, subtitles, and provider content policy. Report findings and propose revisions without automatically applying paid changes.

When eligible public metrics exist, compare 48-hour, 7-day and 28-day observations to the pre-registered hypothesis and comparable channel baselines. Distinguish correlation from causation, missing data from zero, and suggest controlled follow-up experiments.
